A Laredo buyer is out $28,000 after a GMC Sierra purchased through an online marketplace turned out to be stolen, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

The buyer paid $28,000 for a 2025 GMC Sierra, described as fully loaded and four-wheel drive. When the vehicle was brought to the Laredo Police Department's Auto Theft Task Force for a 68-A inspection, investigators determined it was stolen and seized it — leaving the buyer without the truck and without the money, according to the report.

Laredo Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez said the case shows the risk of buying vehicles online at prices that seem unusually low. "It was too good to be true," Rodriguez said, according to the report.

Rodriguez warned buyers to be cautious with online marketplaces such as Facebook Marketplace and Craigslist, and advised sellers to verify a buyer's identity when identification or other documents are provided. He said criminals are using increasingly sophisticated methods, including artificial intelligence, to exploit the vehicle-buying process — from locating vehicles and buyers to financing fraud using fake identification and pay stubs.

The department has also worked with federal partners on luxury vehicles obtained through fraud, with U.S. Customs and Border Protection stopping some at the international bridge, according to the report. Rodriguez said the warning matters especially with the holidays approaching.

The LPD Auto Theft Task Force is working with the Austin Police Department on the case, and the information will be provided to the Webb County District Attorney's Office in case there is a prosecution, according to the report. The seller was identified by the task force but was not named in the report, and it did not say whether the seller has been arrested or charged.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "Laredo buyer loses $28,000 after GMC Sierra bought online is seized as stolen," October 30, 2026
